take_homes: The agent's account of its own work is a claim, not a verdict. Use a cold second reader and my own memory of the work to check it.
The rules file is the thing that travels and improves with each pass. Better prompts are not the lasting part.
Where the agent fills gaps, it writes what is typical, not what is true. I should look for those gaps in my pricing brief.

monday.move: Run the pilot-cohort brief with fresh data, ask the agent to write a rules file from it, and run a cold critic on the result
monday.who: me, then the pricing working group gets the brief
monday.stop_condition: The cold critic flags no claim I can't source
monday.blocker: No shared place for context files. The team keeps separate copies, so the rules file would stay mine.

misconception.why: The rules file travels to the next session in a way a good prompt doesn't. I still think prompts matter, but the file is the lasting part.

one_line: The last third is useful, with the rules file, the cold reader and the handoff. The personal-site exercise and the repeated filler slides waste my time.
